newsitem.title: USA: U.S. April trade data shows exports robust--Yellen.
newsitem.headline: U.S. April trade data shows exports robust--Yellen.

text.p: White House economic advisor Janet Yellen said that trade figures issued on Thursday confirm robust growth in U.S. exports.

"The April trade statistics released today confirm that American exports are continuing their robust growth, which has contributed significantly to the overall strength of the economy," Yellen said in a statement.
Exports reached a record $78.4 billion in April, and for the year to April they were 9.3 percent higher than in the same year-earlier period, the Commerce Department said.

Yellen noted that, for the year to date, exports to Mexico were up 23.4 percent from last year, while exports to South America grew 19.5 percent, exports to Canada increased 12.4 percent, and exports to the European Union rose 9.6 percent.
The trade deficit, which expanded to $8.4 billion in April from $7.8 billion in March "reflects the strength of the U.S. economy relative to its major trade partners," she said.

"U.S. competitiveness remains strong as the expansion continues," Yellen said, noting that exports of advanced technology manufactures have risen 14.3 percent for the year to date, and now account for a quarter of all exports.
Compared with the overall size of the economy, the trade deficit in the first quarter of 1997 was 1.4 percent, well below levels during most of the 1980s, she said.
